name: Jon Ossoff

issue_poll.name: Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Georgia poll, Feb 28-Mar 2, 2026, 1,000 Georgia voters (most important issue facing Georgia)
issue_poll.note: No fall 2026 Georgia poll with a published issue ranking was found (AJC/UGA Oct 7-15 and Quantus Oct 15-17 reports gave no issue ranking). Ranks 1-9 are Emerson's closed-list most-important-issue results in order: economy (jobs, inflation, taxes) 35.5%, housing affordability 14.3%, health care 13.8%, threats to democracy 11.1%, crime 7.7%, immigration 7.2%, education 4.8%, abortion access 2.0%, foreign policy 0.3% ('something else' 3.4% dropped). Rank 10 added from the AARP Georgia poll (Fabrizio Ward/Impact Research, Jul 13-16, 2026, 1,060 likely voters; https://www.aarp.org/pri/topics/voter-research/politics/2026-midterm-election-poll-georgia/), where Social Security and Medicare was a top-two voting issue for 22% of voters 50+, the highest-ranked issue not on Emerson's list. AARP's 50+ results (affordability 35%, immigration 27%, democracy 27%) broadly agree with Emerson's top items. National and state issues ranked together.

issues.detail: Repeal Trump tariffs; ban surveillance-based pricing via Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act of 2026.
Lower housing prices by limiting out-of-state companies buying single-family homes (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, already law).
Reverse 2025 Medicaid cuts; extend or make permanent enhanced ACA tax credits; expand Medicaid in Georgia; limit insurer claim denials.
Ban congressional stock trading; ban corporate PACs; vote against measures making it harder for eligible voters to vote, such as added voter ID requirements.
Support law enforcement; target fentanyl trafficking and online child exploitation.
Remove immigrants here illegally who commit crimes (Laken Riley Act, already law); narrow its overbroad provisions; more ICE detention oversight.
Increase federal funding for Georgia HBCUs.
Support federal abortion protections at the Roe v. Wade privacy standard; no bill named.
End the U.S. war with Iran if Democrats win the Senate; more humanitarian aid to Gaza; support Israel's self-defense.
Defend Social Security and Medicare benefits.

plan_caveats: Issue poll is from early March 2026 (pre-primary, all Georgians not likely voters); no fall 2026 Georgia poll with an issue ranking was found. Rank 10 comes from a different poll (AARP, voters 50+ only).
Poll item 'threats to democracy' was mapped to voting access plus government ethics (stock trading and corporate PAC bans); this is a judgment call.

Ossoff campaigned mostly on his record and attacks on Trump/Collins; few forward-looking specifics. Campaign issues text (electjon.com, July 30, 2026) was read via Ballotpedia; its priority bullets mix past accomplishments with goals, and were treated as stated goals.

Grocery price-gouging bill and ACA tax credit position come from a news issue explainer (Atlanta News First, Oct 8, 2026) rather than his own words; the ACA position was phrased as the credits 'should have been' extended.
Tariff repeal and Iran war end are from the Oct 13 Atlanta Press Club debate; the Iran pledge is conditional on a Democratic Senate majority.
Housing rated Partial because the investor-limit law he cites (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act) has already passed; no new housing proposal found.
Immigration rated Partial: points to existing Laken Riley Act and says to fix overbroad provisions without naming which.
Several debate news pages (WABE, Daily Signal) could not be fetched.
